What it does

This act amends Tennessee Code Annotated Section 1-3-105(a) to redefine the term 'person'. The new definition includes corporations, firms, companies, and associations, but expressly excludes artificial intelligence, computer algorithms, software programs, computer hardware, and any type of machine. It takes effect upon becoming law.

Who it applies to

  • The definition of 'person' in Tennessee Code Annotated Section 1-3-105(a) (Sec. 1)

Effective date

Upon becoming a law (Sec. 2)

Key definitions

  • Person: includes a corporation, firm, company, or association; does not include artificial intelligence, a computer algorithm, a software program, computer hardware, or any type of machine (Sec. 1)

Obligations

  • None stated in the text

Prohibitions

  • None stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

not stated in the text

How it affects AI deployment

  • Artificial intelligence, computer algorithms, software programs, computer hardware, and machines are not 'persons' under Tennessee Code Annotated Section 1-3-105(a), so they cannot be treated as legal persons for purposes of that definition (Sec. 1).
  • A corporation, firm, company, or association that deploys AI is a 'person' under the definition, while the AI itself is not (Sec. 1).

Notable exemptions

  • Artificial intelligence, a computer algorithm, a software program, computer hardware, or any type of machine are excluded from the definition of 'person' (Sec. 1).

Compliance steps

  • No compliance steps are stated in the text

AN ACT to amend Tennessee Code Annotated, Title 1, relative to certain conditions of personhood.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE GENERAL ASSEMBLY OF THE STATE OF TENNESSEE:

 SECTION 1. Tennessee Code Annotated, Section 1-3-105(a), is amended by deleting
subdivision (20) and substituting:

 (20) "Person":

 (A) Includes a corporation, firm, company, or association; and

 (8) Does not include artificial intelligence, a computer algorithm, a software
 program, computer hardware, or any type of machine;

 SECTION 2. This act takes effect upon becoming a law, the public welfare requiring it.
